articles.title: 'Not doing justice to their talent': Yuvraj Singh wants Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in ODIs
articles.summary: Former India all-rounder Yuvraj Singh believes young batters Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi deserve more opportunities in 50-over
articles.body: Former India all-rounder Yuvraj Singh believes young batters Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi deserve more opportunities in 50-over cricket.Yuvraj feels that not regularly considering these players for the ODI team does not do justice to their talent. He also hopes they get a place in the squad soon."I would love to see him (Abhishek) in the ODIs, to be honest, and I have said this before that if we are not picking guys like Ishan Kishan, Abhishek and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in 50-over cricket, then somewhere down the line we are not doing justice to their talent," Yuvraj told PTI on the sidelines of an event.Yuvraj has been Abhishek's mentor for several years and has played an important role in the youngster's development.However, the former India all-rounder understands that the presence of experienced players makes it difficult for youngsters to find a place in the team."I understand we have some great players and it is hard to make a spot for them. I think the way they (young batters) are performing, hopefully, they should be in the squad soon. Whatever he (Abhishek) has achieved is because of his hard work, and credit goes to him," he added.Abhishek responds to Yuvraj's 12-ball fifty challengeAbhishek may have looked up to Yuvraj while growing up, but the young India opener is not ready to accept his mentor's challenge of scoring a half-century off just 12 balls.The left-hander made his point after smashing a 38-ball 113 against New Zealand in the third T20I on Tuesday. His innings helped India register a six-wicket win, and he was named Player of the Match.Yuvraj had posted a playful message on social media, saying that he was still waiting to see Abhishek score a fifty off 12 balls.However, Abhishek said such an achievement was not easy and was not something batters planned for."I don't know what cricket he was playing back at that time, but it's not that easy at all," Abhishek said during the presentation ceremony."I would say if any batter wants to go there and bat like that, it's not easy at all. You can't just go and score 50 off 12 balls. It just happens once in a while," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'The Time Is Now' at Eden Park: How Glenn Phillips turned a John Cena moment into Team India's nightmare - WATCH
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The John Cena theme song playing in the background, Glenn Phillips walking out to the middle and then unleashing a stunning assault on India's
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The John Cena theme song playing in the background, Glenn Phillips walking out to the middle and then unleashing a stunning assault on India's bowlers. Eden Park witnessed a spectacle when the New Zealand batter arrived at the crease during the fourth T20I in Auckland on Friday.Phillips walked out to bat after Daryl Mitchell was dismissed off the fifth ball of the third over, bowled by Mayank Yadav. He first exchanged a fist bump with opening batter Finn Allen. As he began walking towards the crease, the DJ played The Time Is Now, John Cena's famous entrance theme.What followed was absolute mayhem.Phillips took the attack to the Indian bowlers and smashed a breathtaking 107 off just 49 balls. His innings included six fours and 10 sixes as New Zealand posted a massive 259/7.Phillips and Bracewell take India apartPhillips found an equally destructive partner in Michael Bracewell, who scored 65 off just 25 balls. The two batters added 115 runs off only 41 deliveries, taking New Zealand past the 200-run mark in the 16th over.Phillips brought up his third T20I century, reaching the landmark in just 46 balls. His power-hitting left the Indian bowlers struggling for answers.New Zealand finished with 259/7, their highest T20I total against India. They then bowled out the visitors' challenge, restricting India to 172/9 to secure an 87-run win.India had already taken an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series, but Phillips' innings helped New Zealand pull one back.IPL lessons help Phillips find consistencyPhillips credited his time in the Indian Premier League for helping him improve his game. He is the leading run-scorer in the ongoing series, with 276 runs from four matches at an average of 92. His tally includes one century and two half-centuries.The 29-year-old did not have a memorable IPL 2026 season with Gujarat Titans. He played only six matches and scored 67 runs, with 25 being his highest score.However, Phillips said the experience gave him valuable lessons and opportunities to work on his batting.“The IPL is a certain beast of its own and the balance of teams being one of eight overseas (players) with only four spots (in the eleven) make it quite tough. So, if you don't go out there and set the world on fire there's always another person waiting in line,” Phillips said in the post-match press conference.He was happy with the facilities and coaching support he received at Gujarat Titans.“At Gujarat, I was very lucky to have some unbelievable facilities, some great coaches and plenty of time to work (on his batting). I also showed in England as well being able to have volume (of runs) under the belt — whether it's red ball or white ball.“Yes, you'd love to score runs in the IPL and you know make a load of cash and that would be fantastic but also there's a lot of learnings that you can take from that place (in the IPL) whether you're playing or not and I think that is also on each individual that is at the IPL or at any other tournament to be able to make the most out of where they go,” he added.Phillips also had a productive Crowe-Thorpe Trophy earlier this year, scoring 181 runs in four innings at an average of 60, including a century. New Zealand won that series 2-1 against England.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Nitish Reddy joins unwanted list after horror outing against New Zealand
articles.summary: Nitish Reddy entered an unwanted record list after an expensive outing with the ball in the fourth T20I against New Zealand in Auckland on Friday,
articles.body: Nitish Reddy entered an unwanted record list after an expensive outing with the ball in the fourth T20I against New Zealand in Auckland on Friday, conceding 64 runs to join an unenviable group of Indian bowlers.Reddy's figures placed him alongside Yuzvendra Chahal and Varun Chakravarthy for the second-most expensive spell by an Indian bowler in T20I cricket. Krishna tops the list with 68 runs conceded against Australia in Guwahati in 2023, while Chahal had leaked 64 against South Africa in Centurion in 2018. Chakravarthy also conceded 64 against England at the Wankhede in 2026.Reddy's expensive outing came as New Zealand piled up a mammoth 259/7 after being asked to bat first. The hosts eventually secured an emphatic 87-run victory, reducing India's series lead to 3-1.The all-rounder was particularly targeted by Glenn Phillips, who smashed him for 32 runs in the 16th over, including four consecutive sixes. Phillips brought up his half-century in 31 balls before accelerating to a 49-ball 107, his third T20I hundred.Reddy eventually dismissed Phillips after the New Zealand batter had crossed the three-figure mark, but the damage had already been done.Phillips and Michael Bracewell (65 off 25 balls) added 115 runs off just 41 deliveries for the fifth wicket, powering New Zealand to the highest T20I total against India.Most runs conceded by India in overs 11-20 in a T20I151 South Africa Guwahati 2022150 New Zealand Auckland 2026146 England Southampton 2026India's bowling struggles were not limited to Reddy. The visitors conceded 151 runs in the middle overs (11-20), the second-most by India in that phase of a T20I.South Africa hold the record with 151 runs in Guwahati in 2022, while New Zealand's 150 in Auckland took the second spot in the list, followed by England's 146 in Southampton in 2026.India's reply never gathered momentum as Jacob Duffy struck twice in the opening over, removing Sanju Samson and Ishan Kishan. The visitors eventually finished at 172/9, suffering an 87-run defeat.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Jemimah Rodrigues returns after hamstring injury, joins Mumbai squad in Pune
articles.summary: MUMBAI: India women's team batter Jemimah Rodrigues has recovered from a hamstring injury that had kept her out of action for three months and has joined
articles.body: MUMBAI: India women's team batter Jemimah Rodrigues has recovered from a hamstring injury that had kept her out of action for three months and has joined the Mumbai team in Pune for the ongoing Senior Women's T20 Elite domestic tournament.She will now turn out for Mumbai in their remaining matches in the tournament.The development means that Rodrigues is set to return to action for the Indian women's team during their multi-format tour of South Africa in December.“Life Update: HAMSTRING HAS BEEN DECLARED FIT!!!!!!!! After 3 months of rehab. Now I can’t wait to get going,” Jemimah wrote on her Instagram account on Friday.The 26-year-old tore her right hamstring while playing for Southern Brave against Welsh Fire in The Hundred in England earlier this year. Scans at the BCCI Centre of Excellence later confirmed a high-grade tear, which meant that Jemimah was ruled out of the Women's T20 Asia Cup in the UAE, the Asian Games in Japan and India's recently concluded white-ball series against Zimbabwe at home.Ironically, Jemimah's return to fitness comes on the first anniversary of her scoring an unbeaten 127 against Australia in the ODI World Cup semifinal at the DY Patil Stadium in Navi Mumbai. Riding on that innings, India went on to win the trophy.The Indian women's team's tour of South Africa will include a one-off Test, three ODIs and three T20Is.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Nemesis No. 1! Mitchell Santner scripts history, enters record books against India
articles.summary: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner etched his name in the record books during the fourth T20I against India in Auckland on Friday, becoming the leading
articles.body: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner etched his name in the record books during the fourth T20I against India in Auckland on Friday, becoming the leading wicket-taker against India in the shortest format.Santner achieved the landmark after dismissing Nitish Kumar Reddy, taking his tally to 32 wickets in 31 T20Is against India. He surpassed compatriot Ish Sodhi, who has claimed 30 wickets, to move to the top of the list.Most T20I wickets vs India31 Mitchell Santner30 Ish Sodhi24 Chris Jordan22 Jofra Archer/Adil RashidSantner's latest scalp also marked another milestone in his T20I career as he became only the third New Zealand player to reach 150 wickets in the format. He now has 151 wickets from 142 matches at an average of 23.09, including four four-wicket hauls and best figures of 4/11.Mitchell Santner's tally against India includes two four-wicket hauls, with his best figures being 4/11. Australia's Chris Jordan follows with 24 wickets, while England's Jofra Archer and Adil Rashid have 22 wickets each.Santner returned figures of 2/24 in the fourth T20I, also dismissing Axar Patel, as New Zealand registered their first victory of the five-match series with an emphatic 87-run win. His nine wickets in the ongoing series have come at an average of 11.22.Glenn Phillips' blistering 107 off 49 balls and Michael Bracewell's 65 off 25 powered New Zealand to 259/7, the highest T20I total against India. Jacob Duffy then claimed four wickets as India were restricted to 172/9, leaving the visitors with a 3-1 series lead ahead of the final match.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ryan Rickelton, Wiaan Mulder hundreds put South Africa in driver's seat, set 288-run target for Australia in series decider
articles.summary: Centuries from Ryan Rickelton and Wiaan Mulder put South Africa in a commanding position against Australia in the series-deciding third Test at Newlands
articles.body: Centuries from Ryan Rickelton and Wiaan Mulder put South Africa in a commanding position against Australia in the series-deciding third Test at Newlands on Friday, setting up an intriguing final day's play.South Africa, who began the fourth day with a slender 40-run lead and six wickets in hand, finished their second innings on 387, stretching their advantage to 287 runs. Australia now need 288 on the final day to win the three-Test series, which is currently level at 1-1.Rickelton (101 off 219 balls) and Mulder (115 off 221 balls) led South Africa's recovery with a crucial sixth-wicket partnership worth 154 runs. The pair spent nearly 54 overs together, frustrating the Australian bowlers and forcing the visitors to turn to as many as eight bowling options.South Africa were 140/4 overnight and lost Matthew Breetzke in the morning session, caught at fine leg off Pat Cummins. The Australian captain's breakthrough ended a wicketless spell of more than 62 overs stretching back to the first Test in Durban.Rickelton and Mulder then took charge, adding 92 runs during the second session without losing a wicket. Rickelton reached his half-century off 105 deliveries, while Mulder went into the tea break unbeaten on 46. Their partnership crossed the 100-run mark after 193 balls.Australia managed to slow the scoring after tea, conceding just 13 runs in 10 overs, but the South African duo continued to build their lead. Rickelton eventually completed his third Test century off 219 balls, striking 12 boundaries. It was also the first century by a South African batter at No. 6 in the third or fourth innings of a Test since 2022.The partnership ended in unfortunate fashion when Mulder ran out Rickelton after sending him back too late. South Africa then suffered a brief collapse, losing four wickets for just 16 runs, with Gerald Coetzee also falling to a run-out after a mix-up involving Mulder.With the lower order exposed, Mulder took responsibility and shifted gears. Having taken 138 balls to reach his first 50, he needed only another 66 deliveries for his second half-century. He brought up his fourth Test hundred off 204 balls and finished with 10 fours and four sixes before falling to Cummins in the deep while attempting a pull shot.Mitchell Starc was Australia's most successful bowler in the innings, claiming 3/65 to take his match tally to nine wickets.Australia face a challenging chase on the final day, with Newlands having witnessed a successful fourth-innings target of 331 only once, when Australia achieved it in 2002. South Africa will also draw confidence from a pitch expected to offer increasing assistance to spinners and the presence of an in-form Simon Harmer, who was rested earlier in the match.The visitors have the entire fifth day to chase 288 and clinch the series, while South Africa will look to defend their total.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: IPL 2027: Rohit Sharma likely to lead Mumbai Indians again, Tilak Varma could be deputy
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Will Rohit Sharma return as Mumbai Indians captain, with India’s rising T20 batting star Tilak Varma as his deputy, in IPL 2027?
articles.body: MUMBAI: Will Rohit Sharma return as Mumbai Indians captain, with India’s rising T20 batting star Tilak Varma as his deputy, in IPL 2027? TOI has learnt that there is a strong possibility of the 39-year-old getting one final stint at the helm. Rohit led MI to all five of their IPL titles — in 2013, 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2020.A return to the captaincy would mean Rohit cannot feature as an Impact Player, as he has done over the past two seasons. Meanwhile, Hardik Pandya, who replaced Rohit as captain in 2024, is set to be traded to another franchise.MI are in talks with three teams, with an official announcement expected soon, TOI has learnt.MI on Friday announced a major overhaul of their coaching staff under newly appointed head coach Kieron Pollard. Former India batter Robin Uthappa has been named batting coach, while former India fielding coach T Dilip will take charge of the fielding department.Uthappa represented MI in the inaugural IPL season in 2008, while Dilip spent nearly five years with the Indian team and is believed to share a close rapport with Rohit.MI have also brought back two former pacers — New Zealand’s Mitchell McClenaghan as bowling coach and Dhawal Kulkarni as development bowling coach. Kulkarni, a former India and Mumbai teammate of Rohit, will have a year-round role focused on player development and strengthening the franchise’s talent pool.The appointments, with several members of the new support staff having close links with Rohit, have further fuelled speculation about his return to the captaincy as MI look to end their six-year title drought. The franchise last won the IPL in 2020 and finished ninth in 2026. The new coaching group’s immediate task will be to finalise retentions ahead of the mini-auction for IPL 2027, scheduled for Dec 16 in Goa. Pollard and his team will also have to formulate their auction strategy as MI seek to rebuild after a disappointing 2026 campaign.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: India's first women's Test 50 years ago: 22,000 fans, Shantha Rangaswamy's historic six and a landmark draw against West Indies
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Women’s cricket in India has had its share of twists and turns. Its journey into Test cricket was no different.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Women’s cricket in India has had its share of twists and turns. Its journey into Test cricket was no different. Although cricket had been introduced in the country much earlier, the first women’s national championship was held only in April 1973. The game was still finding its feet, with teams playing two and three-day red-ball matches. An Australian team toured India in 1975, and in February the following year, India travelled to New Zealand for a five-match ‘Test series’, which was subsequently deemed unofficial.The first women’s Test, between Australia and England, had been played in Brisbane in 1934. India had to wait another 42 years to make its official debut. That moment unfolded at the KSCA Stadium (renamed the M Chinnaswamy Stadium in 1987), when India hosted West Indies in the first of a six-Test series in October 1976.Led by Louise Browne, the visiting side took on Shantha Rangaswamy’s India in a three-day contest that began on October 31. For the women cricketers, it was a landmark moment.Recalling the occasion, Shantha said: “We had already played a couple of series against Australia and New Zealand, which were later deemed unofficial. So, we weren’t sure until later whether this match would count as an official one.”With one section of the stadium under renovation, the remaining stands were packed, with more than 22,000 spectators turning up. India’s line-up featured some of the rising stars of the game, including Diana Edulji, Shubhangi Kulkarni and Ujwala Nikam.Among those soaking in the atmosphere was former Indian wicketkeeper Kalpana Venkatachar, then a Karnataka age-group cricketer. She was part of a group of young women cricketers who volunteered at the match, handing out scorecards to spectators.“Back in the day, spectators also did the scoring. They watched, tracked and recorded every ball and run in a booklet provided to them. Our job was to hand out these booklets. The excitement was infectious and the crowd was boisterous,” Kalpana recalled.West Indies, who batted first, were bowled out for 274 in 78.4 overs. Shubhangi, one of India’s finest spinners, returned figures of 5/48, while Diana picked up two wickets.India’s reply produced two memorable knocks. Opener Shobha Pandit scored 69, but it was skipper Shantha’s gritty 74 that stole the show. Her innings also featured a landmark moment — a six over long-on off Patricia Whittaker, the first maximum by an Indian woman in international cricket and the first at the stadium. The stand where the ball landed has since been named after Shantha.She remembers the innings as an attempt to inject a modern-day T20 flavour into a game that was still played over three days.“With the matches being held over three days, most of them would end in draws. But I wanted to make it interesting and score some quick runs, like they do in T20 cricket now,” she said.India were 269/6 overnight after 99 overs and were looking to add to their total on the final morning. But an unexpected turn of events prompted Shantha to declare.“We came out to bat on the final day only to see wet patches on the pitch. This drew suspicion from the visiting side and the start was delayed. So, I declared in the hope that we could bowl them out.”West Indies declared their second innings at 175/7, setting India a target of 181. The hosts finished on 30/1 at stumps as the historic contest ended in a draw.For Kalpana and the other youngsters watching from the stands, however, the result was secondary. The sight of Shantha clearing the ropes had left a lasting impression.“Watching Shantha score a six made us believe that we could go the distance too,” she said.Indian women have played 42 more Tests in the five decades since that landmark outing. But the first, played in front of a packed crowd, remains special. The series ended in a 1-1 draw with four drawn contests.Indian team: Sandhya Mazumdar, Shobha Pandit, Fowzieh Khalili, Sudha Shah, Shantha Rangaswamy, Ujwala Nikam, Shubhangi Kulkarni, Susan Itticheria, Diana Edulji, Sharmila Chakraborty, Behroze Edulji.Brief scores: West Indies: 274 in 78.4 overs (Louise Browne 28, Gloria Gill 53, Patricia Whittaker 32, Yolande Geddes-Hall 44, Leila Williams 43; Diana Edulji 2-48, Shubhangi Kulkarni 5-48) and 175/7 declared in 64.5 overs (Patricia 29, Leila 56; Sharmila Chakraborty 2-32, Shubhangi 2-28) drew with India: 269/6 declared in 99 overs (Shobha Pandit 69, Fowzieh Khalili 39, Shantha Rangaswamy 74, Shubhangi 26 not out; Leila Williams 2-50, Vivalyn Latty-Scott 3-51) and 30/1 in 17 overs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'It's win or lose': Ryan Rickelton predicts thrilling final-day finish in South Africa-Australia decider
articles.summary: With the series trophy, the No.
articles.body: With the series trophy, the No. 1 spot in the Test rankings and valuable World Test Championship (WTC) points on the line, South Africa and Australia are bracing for a high-stakes finish to their three-match series at Newlands. After a remarkable fightback from the hosts, the series-deciding third Test is delicately poised heading into the final day on Saturday, with South Africa wicketkeeper Ryan Rickelton ruling out the possibility of a stalemate."It's win or lose, I guess. No draw tomorrow. If you had to say that it's going down to the third Test, day five, with all three results on the cards or two results on the cards, yeah, I wouldn't have believed it. It's been a special series," Rickelton said, as quoted by cricinfo.Rickelton, Mulder hundreds power South Africa's fightbackCenturies from Rickelton and Wiaan Mulder helped South Africa recover from a precarious position and set Australia a challenging target of 288 runs to win the series-deciding third Test of the ICC World Test Championship 2025-27.Resuming their second innings at 140/4 on the fourth morning, the hosts eventually reached 387 before being bowled out in 134.4 overs, putting themselves in a strong position to push for a series victory.The foundation of South Africa's recovery was a magnificent 154-run partnership for the sixth wicket between Rickelton and Mulder. Rickelton struck 101 off 219 deliveries, while Mulder contributed 115 off 221 balls. Their stand is the second-highest sixth-wicket partnership by South Africa against Australia in Test cricket.Rickelton warns Australia of challenging fourth-innings chaseRickelton acknowledged that the new ball could present Australia with an opportunity to accelerate their chase, although the slow and deteriorating nature of the pitch could make the task considerably tougher."I just think with that new ball, there's obviously runs available, and there's obviously wickets too. It has been quite slow. If Australia obviously fancy having a go at it, it might just factor into it. For them to bat at effectively threes the whole day will be a big ask, especially on a slower, lower deteriorating wicket," he added.Earlier, South Africa were bowled out for 329 in their first innings before Australia responded with 429, taking a crucial 100-run lead. However, the hosts' second-innings resurgence has turned the contest on its head and left Australia with a challenging fourth-innings target.With the three-match series level at 1-1, both teams have everything to play for on the final day. Australia must chase down 288 to secure the series, while South Africa need 10 wickets to seal a memorable victory on home soil.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘If you want to fit Vaibhav’: Ex-India cricketer's message to Gautam Gambhir-led management on accommodating Sooryavanshi
articles.summary: Former India wicketkeeper Dinesh Karthik believes Abhishek Sharma should be rested rather than Sanju Samson being dropped again if India want to bring
articles.body: Former India wicketkeeper Dinesh Karthik believes Abhishek Sharma should be rested rather than Sanju Samson being dropped again if India want to bring teenage batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi back into the playing XI for the fifth and final T20I against New Zealand.Sooryavanshi missed the fourth T20I in Auckland after Ishan Kishan recovered from the injury that had ruled him out of the previous two matches. The youngster had made an impression in his last appearance, smashing 45 off just 19 balls in the third T20I in Wellington, but did not feature in Friday's match despite India having already secured the series.Karthik feels Samson should not repeatedly be the one making way whenever India look to accommodate Sooryavanshi. Speaking on Cricbuzz, he suggested giving Abhishek a break instead."I know the world will want Vaibhav to play. If they want to play Vaibhav, it has got to be in place of Abhishek, to give him a break, and that is how it should be. Every time there is anything related to Vaibhav, it is always Sanju. If you want to really fit in Vaibhav, Abhishek can take a break. The key word here is break," Karthik said.Samson started the series on a strong note, scoring a match-winning 67 off 33 balls in Christchurch to claim the Player of the Match award. However, he managed scores of 14 and 18 in the following two matches. He was also moved to No. 3 in the third T20I to make room for Sooryavanshi.The debate over India's batting combination comes after their 87-run defeat in the fourth T20I. New Zealand posted a formidable 259/7, courtesy of Glenn Phillips' 107 off 49 balls, before Jacob Duffy's four-wicket haul helped restrict India to 172/9.India have already clinched the five-match series 3-1, with the final T20I offering another opportunity to assess their combinations ahead of the next assignment.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Dhruv Jurel's unbeaten 99 rescues India A after dramatic collapse against New Zealand A
articles.summary: Dhruv Jurel led India's fightback with a determined unbeaten 99 after the visitors suffered a dramatic collapse on the opening day of the second
articles.body: Dhruv Jurel led India's fightback with a determined unbeaten 99 after the visitors suffered a dramatic collapse on the opening day of the second unofficial Test against New Zealand A in Christchurch.Coming into the match after scores of 1 and 2 in the first unofficial Test last week, Jurel responded with a crucial knock that helped India A recover from a precarious position and finish the day with a fighting total.India A were in trouble in the afternoon session after losing three wickets for just six runs in the space of six deliveries. At 160 for 6, with a substantial part of the day's play still remaining, Jurel took charge and first stitched together a 62-run partnership for the seventh wicket with Manav Suthar.After Suthar departed for 22, Jurel continued to hold the innings together, adding an unbeaten 69 runs with Akash Deep. He reached the 90s in the 79th over but chose to remain unbeaten at 99, seeing out the final nine overs until stumps.The visitors had made a steady start despite challenging batting conditions. Yashasvi Jaiswal was dismissed for a duck just four deliveries into the day, trapped lbw by Fraser Sheat, whose late movement troubled the Indian batters throughout the innings.Sai Sudharsan, promoted to open in the absence of KL Rahul, and Devdutt Padikkal then steadied the innings. The pair negotiated the remainder of the opening session, with Sai Sudharsan surviving a couple of close calls against Sheat before settling into his innings.Padikkal, who had scored 199 in the opening game, initially struggled to get going but gradually found his rhythm through a series of fluent drives. He also adjusted his position at the crease to counter the movement, while punishing the shorter deliveries. A cut behind point brought up his half-century in the second session.Sai Sudharsan, meanwhile, looked set for a substantial contribution before edging at a delivery outside off from Jarrod McKay shortly after lunch. His dismissal opened the door for New Zealand A to take control.Sheat led the charge as India A lost three more wickets in quick succession. Padikkal chopped one back onto his stumps, R Smaran, playing his first match of the tour, was trapped lbw first ball after misjudging the movement, while Washington Sundar was beaten by a full delivery.With the innings in danger of falling apart, Jurel had to negotiate the movement and bounce offered by the Christchurch surface. As the seamers began to tire and strayed towards his pads, he found opportunities to score and gradually shifted the momentum.New Zealand A eventually turned to left-arm spinner Jayden Lennox, who was introduced to test Jurel in a batting line-up dominated by right-handers. However, the wicketkeeper-batter used his feet and the crease effectively, mixing sweeps with cuts and dabs to keep the scoreboard moving.Suthar provided valuable support before falling for 22 while attempting a drive off Lennox. Jurel then took responsibility for the lower order, ensuring India A avoided a repeat of their batting struggles in the first innings of the Lincoln match.His unbeaten 99 has given the visitors a measure of stability heading into the second day, with Akash Deep still alongside him at the crease.India A 291 for 7 (Jurel 99*, Padikkal 80, Sheat 4-50) vs New Zealand AGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'I wanted to see my career out with Lancs': James Anderson reveals emotional toll of County exit
articles.summary: James Anderson is still coming to terms with an unexpected end to his 25-year association with Lancashire, admitting that the county's decision not to
articles.body: James Anderson is still coming to terms with an unexpected end to his 25-year association with Lancashire, admitting that the county's decision not to renew his contract has left him questioning his future in cricket. The veteran fast bowler, who had hoped to finish his career at the club he supported as a child, said the experience brought back memories of how his England career came to an end nearly two years ago.The 44-year-old, speaking on the BBC podcast Tailenders, revealed that he has yet to decide whether to find another county or call time on his playing career. Despite the disappointment, Anderson said he was beginning to feel optimistic about the opportunities that lie ahead."I don't know what the end looks like, but obviously I wanted to see my career out with Lancs. I don't know if my career's done, we'll have to wait and see, but it'd be nice, at some point, if someone will let me retire," Anderson said."I'm still sort of trying to process everything, and weigh up what the best way forward for me is, really."Anderson draws parallels between Lancashire and England exitsAnderson's departure from Lancashire came as a surprise despite his impressive individual performances during the County Championship season. The veteran pacer captained the side and claimed 50 wickets, although Lancashire finished second-last in Division Two.Last month, the club's new director of cricket, Paul Farbrace, informed Anderson that his contract would not be renewed for the 2027 season. Reacting to the development, the fast bowler expressed his disappointment on Instagram, writing that "if it was up to me it wouldn't have ended like this."Anderson revealed that he had initially expected a discussion about Lancashire's performances and the team's plans for the future, rather than a conversation about his own departure."I went in for what I thought was a conversation about how the team moves forward, because obviously it wasn't a great year for the team," he said."Being captain, I thought it was sort of just a chat about that. And then a couple of minutes in, I realised it wasn't a conversation; I was just being told that they thought the best way for the team to move forward is without me. Obviously, I was quite shocked. It was quite brief and, yeah, that was it."The decision brought back memories of his England exit, when the team management informed him nearly two years ago that he was no longer part of their plans.'Is there something fundamentally wrong with me?': Anderson opens upThe veteran pacer admitted that Lancashire's decision triggered self-doubt, particularly after he had spent the previous season trying to understand how he could help the team improve.Anderson said he had regularly discussed the team's struggles with the head coach and questioned whether there was anything more he could have done in his role as captain."Last year didn't go too well for us on the field and all the way through the season, myself and the head coach are like, 'Is it something we're doing? Could we be doing more to help the team play better?' I finished the season thinking, 'Was it something I did, but was I doing something wrong?'"And then I get told this news and then I'm thinking that even more. I'm thinking, 'God, this is happening again. Is there something fundamentally wrong with me as a person, as a human being?' But your head just sort of races. I just didn't really know what to make of it for a good week. You're thinking, 'God, I'm never going to play cricket again.' All these sorts of things."Anderson also made it clear that his emotional connection with Lancashire would remain unchanged despite the circumstances of his departure."I am sad the way it ended with the club I supported as a kid but now I have thought about it I am quite excited for the future. I am always going to support Lancashire."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Send him home’: Ex-India cricketer's blunt message to Gautam Gambhir-led team over Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
articles.summary: Former India opener Aakash Chopra has questioned India's decision to drop Vaibhav Sooryavanshi for the fourth T20I against New Zealand, urging the team
articles.body: Former India opener Aakash Chopra has questioned India's decision to drop Vaibhav Sooryavanshi for the fourth T20I against New Zealand, urging the team management to clarify the youngster's role and long-term future in the side.Chopra felt Sooryavanshi should not be viewed merely as a stand-in whenever an established player is unavailable. He also suggested that if the teenager is unlikely to get regular opportunities in the playing XI, he would be better off returning to domestic cricket, particularly first-class cricket, to gain match experience and spend more time batting in the middle.Sooryavanshi got his opportunities in the second and third T20Is after Ishan Kishan was sidelined by an injury. He scored 4 and 45 in those two outings before making way for Kishan, who returned to the side for the fourth match.Chopra pointed out that the fourth T20I was a dead rubber and felt the decision to leave Sooryavanshi out raised questions about India's plans for the youngster."Last match, Abhishek made 100 and Vaibhav missed his 50. But the batting was very good. After that, the question was, if Ishan is fit, who will go out. If you think philosophically, then the answer is Vaibhav Sooryavanshi since he replaced an injured Kishan. But this was a dead rubber," Chopra said on his YouTube channel.He questioned whether Sooryavanshi would only feature when another player was unavailable, adding that regular cricket would be more beneficial if he was not part of India's immediate plans."The decision to drop Vaibhav Sooryavanshi leads to a bigger question. Will you play Vaibhav Sooryavanshi only when someone is injured? Or when someone is unavailable? If that is the case, you can send him home. You can tell him to go and play first-class cricket. Of course, he can learn by staying in the Indian dressing room. But if it's happening for an extended period, he should get bat on ball," he added.Chopra also called on the team management to make its thinking clear, saying that while a roadmap may already be in place, there has been little public clarity about Sooryavanshi's role."The team should come out and share what their roadmap and philosophy is. Maybe they have already thought about it and have already charted out a plan. But they haven't told anybody. As such, we don't know what they are going to do with Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. His absence was a little disappointing," Chopra said.Kishan, meanwhile, had a brief return to the side. He was dismissed for a duck as India failed to chase New Zealand's target of 260, eventually finishing at 172/9.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Pakistan vs Sri Lanka, ODI Tri-Series Final Live Score: Pakistan and Sri Lanka clash in ODI tri-series final
articles.body: The late collapse - That wicket of Kamindu started the downfall. Dasun Shanaka began brightly, connecting well, but Afridi cleared the danger before it became serious. Haris Rauf then removed Pavan, who had reached his second ODI fifty, and the wickets tumbled as the run rate dipped, with Sri Lanka slipping to 307 for 8, before Asitha Fernando and Maheesh Theekshana did their best to pull the score to 325. Sri Lanka have posted a 326 target, their best ever at the Gaddafi Stadium! But is it enough on a flat pitch? Only time will tell! Stick with us as the second innings will start in sometime.. Agha breaks through - Just after the drinks break, Salman Ali Agha got the breakthrough by removing Fernando, and he struck again soon after to dismiss Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis. Pakistan thought they were back in it, but Kamindu and Pavan added a huge partnership that lifted the score from 109 for 2 to 255 for 2. Kamindu brought up his maiden ODI century on the way and went on to 131, before Shaheen Afridi returned and removed him with the very first ball of his new spell.. Fernando and Kamindu set the tone - Pakistan won the toss and chose to bowl, wanting the fresh wicket and hoping to escape the late dew in Lahore, but just when the match started, the pitch looked dead instantly. Avishka Fernando and Kamindu Mendis made them pay, batting positively and punishing anything loose to take Sri Lanka to 86 without loss after 16 overs. The spinners found a little turn, but clear chances were rare, and Kamindu survived a caught-behind appeal against Arafat Minhas that was overturned on review.. Pakistan pull It back - What a rollercoaster this innings has been! On a belter of a pitch, Sri Lanka were calling the shots, but Pakistan refused to panic. Six wickets in the last nine overs, and just when the batters were looking to cash in, the innings came crashing down. However, the tailenders have done what they could and stretched the score to 325, losing eight wickets..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 325/8 (49.6 overs) 49.6: Haris Rauf to Asitha Fernando, The batters run two, but only one run is added to the total as the umpire feels there is a short run taken by Asitha Fernando. So, Sri Lanka finish with 325/8 on the board. Full and on off, Fernando digs it out to deep cover and the batters race back for the second run, which isn't going to be counted because, while turning, Fernando didn't ground his bat inside the popping crease..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 324/8 (49.5 overs) 49.5: Haris Rauf to Maheesh Theekshana, Good work in the deep, and the batters only get a single. Short and angled down leg, Maheesh Theekshana moves well inside the line and hoicks it down to the right of deep backward square leg. Babar Azam cuts it off well, but Theekshana is admiring his shot and thinks he's got a boundary here but that doesn't allow him to get back for the second run..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 323/8 (49.4 overs) 49.4: Haris Rauf to Asitha Fernando, The batters steal a run here. Full and just outside off, Asitha Fernando makes room to go through the off side but misses. Maheesh Theekshana is already on his bike and the keeper misses the under-arm throw at the striker's end..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 322/8 (49.3 overs) 49.3: Haris Rauf to Maheesh Theekshana, Only a single. Maheesh tries to back away but Rauf follows him with a quick ball, bowling it back of a length and this is nudged away behind square leg for a single..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 321/8 (49.2 overs) 49.2: Haris Rauf to Maheesh Theekshana, A good bumper! Quick and over off and middle, at an awkward height as well. Theekshana just ducks under it..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 321/8 (49.1 overs) 49.1: Haris Rauf to Maheesh Theekshana, Swing and a miss! Back of a length and around off, shoots up off the deck. Maheesh Theekshana looks to pull it over mid-wicket but fails to connect..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 321/8 (48.6 overs) 48.6: Naseem Shah to Asitha Fernando, FOUR! Edged away, but Asitha won't mind it at all. Full ball around off, Asitha Fernando backs away and goes hard at it, getting an outside edge that goes wide of the keeper and into the deep third fence..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 317/8 (48.5 overs) 48.5: Naseem Shah to Maheesh Theekshana, Full and around off, pushed away into the off side for a single..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 316/8 (48.5 overs) 48.5: Naseem Shah to Maheesh Theekshana, Wide! Another short ball, slower and just angling down leg. Theekshana ducks under it and another wide is called..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 315/8 (48.5 overs) 48.5: Naseem Shah to Maheesh Theekshana, Wide! Banged in short and angled down leg..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 314/8 (48.4 overs) 48.4: Naseem Shah to Maheesh Theekshana, SIX! That's come out of nowhere! Pitched up around off, at a gentle pace as well. Maheesh Theekshana holds his shape well and thwacks it over long off for a biggie..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 308/8 (48.3 overs) 48.3: Naseem Shah to Asitha Fernando, Skiddy length, pushed through quicker over middle. Fernando chops it down towards leg slip and picks up a single..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 307/8 (48.2 overs) 48.2: Naseem Shah to Asitha Fernando, Another slower ball, into the deck and angled into the batter. Asitha Fernando backs away to open up the off side but fails to lay a bat on it.. Asitha Fernando walks up next..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 307/8 (48.1 overs) 48.1: Naseem Shah to Sahan Arachchige, OUT! CAUGHT! A wonderful change of pace by Naseem Shah, and Sri Lanka keep losing steam at the death, slipping from 279/3 to now 307/8. This is dug into the deck, shorter and slower, angling it across off. Sahan Arachchige has a bit too much time on his hands and eventually tries to just ramp it over short third. But, there's no pace on the ball and it gets lobbed down to short third where Faheem Ashraf takes a simple catch.. Maheesh Theekshana takes a nasty blow to his helmet. The physio comes in for a mandatory concussion check. Everything looks good to continue. Also, Pakistan are penalized for a slower over rate, and will be allowed a maximum of only 4 fielders outside the inner ring..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 307/7 (47.6 overs) 47.6: Haris Rauf to Maheesh Theekshana, Ouch! That's a nasty blow on the helmet. Haris Rauf bowls another sharp bumper, right at the batter and this one rears up off the deck. Maheesh Theekshana is unable to completely duck under it and gets hit flush on the helmet. The ball lobs down to fine leg and the batters get a couple of leg byes. Hopefully, Theekshana is fine here..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 305/7 (47.5 overs) 47.5: Haris Rauf to Maheesh Theekshana, Well bowled! An aggressive bumper, right at the batter, and Maheesh Theekshana has to duck under it.. Maheesh Theekshana is the next batter..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 305/7 (47.4 overs) 47.4: Haris Rauf to Dunith Wellalage, OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Good review! Rauf bangs it in shorter and over off, at an awkward height. Dunith Wellalage tries to rise up on his toes and cuts but feathers it through to Saad Baig. Edged and gone, or is it? The bowler and the keeper start celebrating, but the umpire doesn't raise his finger. Haris Rauf is absolutely certain and Shaheen Afridi reviews it. The third umpire has a look at it and finds on UltraEdge that Wellalage ran the ball off the face of the blade, and the on-field decision is overturned. Pakistan keep getting timely wickets at the death..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 305/6 (47.3 overs) 47.3: Haris Rauf to Sahan Arachchige, Back of a length and around off, tighter line. Arachchige backs away and mictimes the cut through the short third region for a single..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 304/6 (47.2 overs) 47.2: Haris Rauf to Sahan Arachchige, FOUR! Swung away to the fence. Hard length on off, angling in. Arachchige moves inside the line, uses the angle well and heaves it wide of mid-wicket for a boundary..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 300/6 (47.1 overs) 47.1: Haris Rauf to Dunith Wellalage, Full of a good length, speared in towards the stumps. Dunith Wellalage stays leg side of the ball and bunts it to the off side for a single. 300 up for Sri Lanka..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 299/6 (46.6 overs) 46.6: Naseem Shah to Dunith Wellalage, Another single to end, 8 runs and a wicket off the over. Full and on the legs, angling down, Wellalage flicks it down to deep backward square leg and crosses over..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 298/6 (46.5 overs) 46.5: Naseem Shah to Sahan Arachchige, Shah nails the yorker now, on off and middle. Arachchige stays back and jams it towards cover for one more. This has been a good comeback from Naseem Shah in this over..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 297/6 (46.4 overs) 46.4: Naseem Shah to Dunith Wellalage, Wider on the crease again, very full and slanted into the pads. Dunith Wellalage gets squared up and edges it down through the gully region for a single.. Dunith Wellalage is the new man at the crease..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 296/6 (46.3 overs) 46.3: Naseem Shah to Janith Liyanage, OUT! CAUGHT! Crunched, but straight to the fielder in the deep. Naseem Shah bowls it seam-up, going full and wide outside off. Janith Liyanage stays deep in his crease and smacks it flat but straight down the throat of the fielder at deep point. Maaz Sadaqat takes a sharp reverse-cup catch around his face, and Sri Lanka lose yet another wicket, slipping down to 296/6 now..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 296/5 (46.2 overs) 46.2: Naseem Shah to Sahan Arachchige, Shah comes around the wicket now, angling it in from wider on the crease. A bit short and on off, Arachchige presses back and dabs it in front of mid-wicket for a single..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 295/5 (46.1 overs) 46.1: Naseem Shah to Sahan Arachchige, FOUR! Naseem starts off with a slower one yet again and gets punished. Full and outside off, Arachchige drills it through extra cover and picks up a welcome boundary..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 291/5 (45.6 overs) 45.6: Shaheen Afridi to Sahan Arachchige, Excellent stuff from Shaheen at the death, only 4 off the over. Full of a good length, banged into the surface and on off. Arachchige stays back and dabs it wide of point for a single..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 290/5 (45.5 overs) 45.5: Shaheen Afridi to Sahan Arachchige, Another dot ball. Full and speared into middle and leg, Sahan Arachchige flicks it sweetly but finds the fielder at mid-wicket once again..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 290/5 (45.4 overs) 45.4: Shaheen Afridi to Sahan Arachchige, Nearly chipped straight to the fielder. Pitched up at the stumps, Arachchige clips it away but gets more of a leading edge in front of the mid-wicket fielder..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 290/5 (45.3 overs) 45.3: Shaheen Afridi to Janith Liyanage, Pace off this time, short and pushed wide of the off stump. Janith Liyanage goes after it and slashes it down to deep backward point for just one more..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 289/5 (45.2 overs) 45.2: Shaheen Afridi to Sahan Arachchige, Top delivery! An inswinging yorker now, landing it right at the toes. Arachchige can't to anything but dig it out into the off side and pick up a single..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 288/5 (45.1 overs) 45.1: Shaheen Afridi to Janith Liyanage, Good-length delivery, pushed into the front pad. Liyanage stabs it down in front of mid on and collects a quick single..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 287/5 (44.6 overs) 44.6: Haris Rauf to Janith Liyanage, Short of a length, outside off, Janith Liyanage guides it to deep backward point for a single..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 286/5 (44.5 overs) 44.5: Haris Rauf to Sahan Arachchige, Yorker, outside off, Sahan Arachchige digs it out to point for one..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 285/5 (44.4 overs) 44.4: Haris Rauf to Janith Liyanage, Shaping down the leg side, on a hard length. Janith Liyanage misses his flick and hits high on the thigh pad before it rolls to backward square leg for a leg bye..Sri Lanka vs Pakistan Live Score : 284/5 (44.3 overs) 44.3: Haris Rauf to Sahan Arachchige, On a length, at the stumps, Sahan Arachchige pushes it wide of bowler and gets a single.. Extra bounce and pace from a hard length outside off, rushing Rathnayake as he attempts to flat-bat down the ground. Undone by the speed off the deck, he can only miscue it high into the sky. Babar Azam judges it nicely at long-on, tracking to his left and getting right underneath to safely complete the catch.. A slight halt in play as Janith Liyanage has hurt himself while putting in a dive at the non-striker's end. The physio has a quick look at it, and Liyanage is good to continue.

articles.title: ‘He cannot set the momentum’: Shardul Thakur explains Shreyas Iyer's batting struggles
articles.summary: Shardul Thakur has backed Shreyas Iyer amid questions over the Indian captain's batting returns in the ongoing T20I series against New Zealand, saying the
articles.body: Shardul Thakur has backed Shreyas Iyer amid questions over the Indian captain's batting returns in the ongoing T20I series against New Zealand, saying the middle-order batter should not be judged on the basis of a handful of performances.India suffered an 87-run defeat in the fourth T20I in Auckland on Friday after failing to chase down New Zealand's target of 260. Iyer contributed 22 off 11 deliveries, but India finished at 172/9.Speaking during a review of the match on SonyLIV, Thakur explained that Iyer's position in the batting order does not always allow him to dictate the tempo, unlike the top-order batters. The all-rounder pointed out that the No. 4 batter often has to adapt to the situation when he walks in."Many times, how you bat depends on the match situation, and at the number he bats, he has to react to the situation. He cannot set the momentum. The momentum gets set by the top three batters, but Shreyas Iyer comes at No. 4, and sometimes at No. 5 if the left-hander is sent in as a tactical call," he said.Thakur added that batting in the middle order brings its own challenges, as Iyer has to assess the scoreboard, build his innings and also deliver towards the end."You have to react based on the situation and the scoreboard. So it's not an easy position to bat, and once you get set, you also need death batting. So, it's a challenge as to how you adapt to the game, set the tempo of your batting, and finish as well. So he has a lot of responsibility," Thakur observed.Iyer has scored 76 runs in the first four matches of the series at an average of 19. He began with a 42 off 28 balls in the opening T20I but managed only single-digit scores in the next two games before making 22 in Auckland.Thakur also highlighted the additional demands of leading the Indian side, saying captaincy can influence a player's decision-making. However, he pointed to Iyer's leadership record in the IPL as evidence of his ability to handle the responsibility."On top of that, he is the captain. That's an added responsibility for him these days. So the decision-making can be up and down at times. However, we have seen him doing captaincy in domestic cricket and especially in the IPL, and he has played the final with two (three) franchises. He played the final with KKR and won. He played the final with Punjab and lost," he said.The Mumbai Indians all-rounder further backed Iyer's progress as India's captain, recalling that he had made a strong recovery after a difficult start to his stint in the role. Thakur urged against drawing conclusions about a player's or captain's abilities based on fluctuations in the shortest format."So he has the captaincy skills, and he is showing that when he is leading the Indian team. His start wasn't good, but the comeback he has made in captaincy, and the tactics he is trying to apply in the game are working for him. Ups and downs keep happening in T20 cricket. You don't need to judge any batter or bowler much in this format, and Shreyas Iyer too as a captain," Thakur observed.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Not looking at him for white-ball cricket': Is Ravindra Jadeja's ODI career over?
articles.summary: Former India cricketers Cheteshwar Pujara and Abhishek Nayar have offered different views on Ravindra Jadeja's future in ODI cricket after the all-rounder
articles.body: Former India cricketers Cheteshwar Pujara and Abhishek Nayar have offered different views on Ravindra Jadeja's future in ODI cricket after the all-rounder was left out of some recent series.The 37-year-old was not included in India's squad for the five-match ODI series against New Zealand, with Axar Patel currently the team's first-choice left-arm finger spinner. With the ODI World Cup a year away and Jadeja missing out on selection for overseas conditions, questions have been raised about his chances of making the squad for the tournament.Pujara feels Jadeja's exclusion could signal the end of his ODI career, with Axar ahead of him in the team's plans."I believe so, because if you want to keep Ravindra Jadeja in ODI cricket, then he should have been selected. I'm sure it was communicated to him that he might not be selected because Axar Patel has been the main all-rounder in ODI cricket and is being given more opportunities."Looking at his age, I feel the team management might have told him that he is now only a part of Test cricket, so he should focus there, and that they are not looking at him for white-ball cricket. So, it could be the end of the road because, obviously, he has retired from T20 Internationals. I feel he might not be selected just for the ODIs," Pujara told JioStar, as quoted by news agency IANS.Nayar, however, believes Jadeja could still be part of India's plans as a backup for Axar at the World Cup. He described the senior all-rounder as an "insurance policy" for the team in case Axar is unavailable."Jaddu might not come back into the team, but if someone gets injured, the first name that will come to mind will be Jaddu. Because after Axar, there is no one."The valid question right now would be: After Axar, who is the frontrunner? Currently, the frontrunner is Axar Patel, and after him, Jaddu is still your insurance policy. If something happens to Axar Patel before the World Cup, Ravindra Jadeja will come into the team," he said on the same show.India's ODI series against New Zealand begins on November 4. The series will give the team an opportunity to test its combinations against a strong opponent in challenging conditions as it prepares for next year's World Cup, which will be held in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Where Allan Donald and Morkel couldn't: Kagiso Rabada joins Steyn and Pollock in elite Test club
articles.summary: Kagiso Rabada struck twice in the first over of Australia's fourth-innings chase on Saturday, putting South Africa in control of the third Test in Cape
articles.body: Kagiso Rabada struck twice in the first over of Australia's fourth-innings chase on Saturday, putting South Africa in control of the third Test in Cape Town. Australia began the final day's play needing 288 runs to win the match and the series, but Rabada removed opener Matt Renshaw and No. 3 batter Marnus Labuschagne in the first over to leave the visitors in early trouble.Two wickets in the 1st over of a Test innings for SA:Allan Donald vs IND, Durban, 1996 (4th inns)Dale Steyn vs NZ, Centurion, 2016 (4th inns)Morne Morkel vs BAN, Potchefstroom, 2017 (4th inns)Kagiso Rabada vs AUS, Cape Town, 2026 (4th inns)*Rabada became only the fourth South African bowler to take two wickets in the first over of a Test innings. The previous instances were Allan Donald against India in Durban in 1996, Dale Steyn against New Zealand in Centurion in 2016 and Morne Morkel against Bangladesh in Potchefstroom in 2017. All three instances, like Rabada's, came in the fourth innings.Rabada then dismissed Travis Head with the final ball of the seventh over to reduce Australia to three wickets down. Bowling at 143 kmph, Rabada delivered a full ball outside off stump. Head went for a drive without moving his feet and edged it towards gully, where Marco Jansen took the catch with both hands.Head's dismissal also brought up Rabada's 350th Test wicket, making him only the fourth South African bowler to reach the milestone. Dale Steyn leads the list with 439 wickets, followed by Shaun Pollock (421) and Makhaya Ntini (390). Allan Donald finished his Test career with 330 wickets, while Morne Morkel took 309.FOLLOW LIVEEarlier, centuries from Wiaan Mulder and Ryan Rickelton helped South Africa recover on Day 4 and set Australia a target of 288. The hosts were bowled out for 387 in their second innings in the final over of the day, having conceded a 100-run lead in the first innings.Rickelton scored 101 off 219 balls, while Mulder made 115 off 221 deliveries to put South Africa in a position to challenge Australia for the series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: World record at 40! Sikandar Raza smashes unbeaten ton against Afghanistan, enters elite list
articles.summary: Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza created history with a stunning unbeaten century against Afghanistan in the second T20I in Sharjah on Thursday.
articles.body: Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza created history with a stunning unbeaten century against Afghanistan in the second T20I in Sharjah on Thursday. The 40-year-old scored 106 not out off just 56 balls, hitting five fours and nine sixes.However, his brilliant effort could not prevent Zimbabwe from losing by 19 runs as Afghanistan secured an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series.Raza became the first Zimbabwean batter to score two centuries in T20 internationals. He also made history as the oldest batter from a Full Member nation to score a T20I century, achieving the feat at 40 years and 188 days.Germany's Mussadiq Ahmed remains the first player overall to score a T20I hundred at the age of 40, having made 122 against Austria earlier this year.Oldest T20I centurions from full member nationsPlayerCountryMatch Date & OpponentVenueAgeScoreSikandar RazaZimbabwe29/10/2026 vs AfghanistanSharjah40 years 188 days106*Brendan TaylorZimbabwe28/09/2025 vs BotswanaHarare39 years 234 days123Rohit SharmaIndia17/01/2024 vs AfghanistanBengaluru36 years 262 days121*Chris GayleWest Indies16/03/2016 vs EnglandMumbai36 years 177 days100*Jos ButtlerEngland11/07/2026 vs IndiaThe Rose Bowl35 years 306 days131Morne van WykSouth Africa14/01/2015 vs West IndiesDurban35 years 300 days114*Zimbabwe were struggling at 82 for five while chasing Afghanistan's total when Raza stepped up to lead the fightback. He joined debutant Tafadzwa Tsiga, and the pair put together an unbeaten 120-run partnership for the sixth wicket. Tsiga contributed 31 not out from 23 balls, but Zimbabwe could only manage 202 for five, falling short of the target.Afghanistan recover from early collapseEarlier, Zimbabwe's bowlers had put Afghanistan under serious pressure after reducing them to 38 for five. Brad Evans struck twice in the opening over, dismissing Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Mohammad Akram. Kundai Matigimu then removed Ibrahim Zadran and Shahidullah with his first two deliveries. Debutant Vincent Masekesa also claimed a wicket as Afghanistan slipped to 45 for five at the halfway stage.However, Azmatullah Omarzai and Ijaz Ahmad Ahmadzai turned the game around with a 142-run partnership for the sixth wicket. Their attacking batting helped Afghanistan reach 221 for seven, scoring 176 runs in the final 10 overs.Meanwhile, Rashid Khan made history of his own by becoming the first bowler in men's T20I cricket to take 200 wickets.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Amol Muzumdar hints at specialist T20I squad for India women: 'Not long'
articles.summary: Indian women's cricket team have been excellent in Test and ODI formats in recent times.
articles.body: Indian women's cricket team have been excellent in Test and ODI formats in recent times. Under former captain Harmanpreet Kaur, they won four of their last five Tests, a big feat considering that only four countries play Test cricket in the women's game. They are also the reigning Women's ODI World Cup champions, having clinched their maiden title almost exactly a year ago.However, their T20I game still needs improvement. India were knocked out in the league stage of the 2024 and 2026 T20 World Cups. In the shortest format, the team needs to improve on many fronts.Head coach Amol Muzumdar believes India could soon have a specialist T20I squad, similar to the men's team, with the next generation of cricketers better equipped to meet the demands of the format. Asked how soon that could become a reality, Muzumdar replied: “Not long.”“We’re already on that path. There’s some amazing talent coming through. The talent I’ve seen at the CoE (Centre of Excellence), where they hold the India Under-15 and U-19 camps, is terrific. The work at the CoE is superb. The camps are a good reflection of where Indian women’s cricket is at the moment. I’m sure it’s in a healthy state,” he said at an event organised by the Sports Journalists’ Association of Mumbai (SJAM) at the MIG Club on Saturday.Muzumdar believes the next generation could speed up that transition. Having grown up with the demands of modern T20 cricket, these players have a better understanding of the importance of nutrition, fitness and fielding.“They are tuned in. They are professionals. Even the U-15 players are professionals. They understand the nutrition aspect of the game. They understand the fitness aspect of the game. They understand fielding. They’re terrific fielders. They’re good athletes. They understand that athleticism is key in cricket. You’ll soon find that when the younger generation takes over, India will be in a good state,” he said.The coach also said that a player's willingness to learn was as important to him as their skill. “I see whether he or she is receptive. If he or she is receptive, you know it from their body language. You need to learn to understand the body language of the player. Over the years, I have spent a few years in First-Class cricket, and I do understand that I can know a certain player through their body language on the ground. I try to catch those signals. There is always that correct timing of that advice that has to be given. So as a coach, you need to understand when to say, how to say and what to say,” he felt.Muzumdar said he was also conscious of giving players the space they needed. “Sometimes you have to respect the space that the athlete wants. You can have 10,000 things as a coach to tell that athlete. But whether he or she is in that time frame or the mind frame to understand what you are doing...” he said.A year after India won their maiden Women's ODI World Cup title, beating South Africa in the final at the DY Patil Stadium in Navi Mumbai on November 2, Muzumdar recalled the team spirit that marked the campaign. He credited the unity within the squad and the atmosphere in the dressing room for helping the team during the tournament.“If I have to pinpoint just one, then I think the unity in the camp and the dressing room atmosphere. Because of that unity, the dressing room atmosphere was very light. There was a little bit of a buzz around in the dressing room, which I love to create,” he said.Muzumdar compared that atmosphere to the Mumbai teams he played for in the 1990s, which won the Ranji Trophy several times during that period.“I have played in such teams where whenever we have done well, what I am talking about in the 90s, when we did well, just the dressing room atmosphere was phenomenal. There was some kind of a buzz triggered to the kind of cricket that was reflected on the ground. So I think if I have to pinpoint one, it is unity in the camp and just the buzz in the dressing room,” he said.Having worked closely with Harmanpreet during his three-year tenure, Muzumdar praised the outgoing captain and said he was looking forward to working with new skipper Smriti Mandhana.“I had a very good time with Harman as a captain. But I’m also looking forward to the future. With utmost respect, the manner in which she conducted herself as a captain, as a skipper, was superb. I feel myself really lucky that I had that opportunity for the three years that I spent with her as a coach. I could gather the mindset of the captain... I could gather the mindset of the leader in her. I consider myself really lucky about it,” he said.Muzumdar said he wanted to build a culture of dominance and ruthlessness on the field in the Indian women's team.“Dominance is something that we have always spoken about within the squad. Being ruthless on the ground is another thing that we have always maintained. I don’t know where it stems from,” he said.Much of Muzumdar's coaching philosophy comes from his formative years in Mumbai cricket. The former domestic stalwart said he wanted to pass on those lessons to the Indian women's team.“Obviously, from the background where I come, the kind of majority growth in Mumbai cricket was similar. I try to inculcate those things or give it back. If we start dominating world cricket, I would be happy.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Brandon King's 81 not out guides West Indies to 1-0 series lead against Bangladesh
articles.summary: West Indies defeated Bangladesh by eight wickets in the first Test after chasing down a target of 170 runs on Saturday.
articles.body: West Indies defeated Bangladesh by eight wickets in the first Test after chasing down a target of 170 runs on Saturday.Opener Brandon King led the charge with an unbeaten 81 off 115 balls, hitting 10 fours and a six. Kavem Hodge supported him with an unbeaten 31 as West Indies comfortably secured a 1-0 lead in the two-match series.West Indies' spinners played a major role in the win, bowling Bangladesh out for just 142 in their second innings.Captain Roston Chase picked up five wickets for 36 runs, while Jomel Warrican claimed four for 63. Warrican had also taken five wickets in Bangladesh's first innings.Bangladesh resumed Day 4 at 79 for six but managed only 63 more runs. Nayeem Hasan top-scored with 52, recording his maiden Test half-century, but Chase eventually dismissed him to complete his five-wicket haul.King and Campbell lead the chaseChasing 170 on a difficult pitch, West Indies openers Brandon King and John Campbell chose to attack rather than defend against Bangladesh's spinners.The pair added 112 runs for the first wicket, putting their team in a strong position. King brought up his sixth Test half-century, while Campbell scored 49 after making 54 in the first innings.Shoriful Islam dismissed Campbell with a swinging delivery, while Hasan Mahmud removed Tagenarine Chanderpaul for one.However, Bangladesh could not create further pressure as King and Hodge added an unbeaten 50-run partnership to finish the chaseEarlier, Bangladesh scored 272 in their first innings before West Indies replied with 245. The second Test will be played in Sylhet next week, with Bangladesh looking to level the series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'UAE se haare': Pakistan PM gets fact-checked by ex-India cricketer after 'victory over India' post
articles.summary: Former India cricketer Aakash Chopra took a sarcastic dig at Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif after he congratulated the Pakistan team for their
articles.body: Former India cricketer Aakash Chopra took a sarcastic dig at Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif after he congratulated the Pakistan team for their victory over India in the 2026 Hong Kong Sixes tournament. Chopra pointed out that Pakistan had lost its opening match against the United Arab Emirates (UAE).Pakistan beat India in the Hong Kong Sixes on Friday, a six-a-side tournament in which each team bats for six overs. Following the win, Sharif took to social media to praise the team and congratulate the players."Congratulations to our boys on a superb four-wicket victory over India in the opening clash of the Hong Kong Sixes 2026! It was a good game of cricket. I also commend Chairman PCB Mohsin Naqvi and his team for their dedicated efforts in preparing and supporting," Sharif wrote on X.Chopra, however, questioned the Pakistan Prime Minister's celebration, pointing out that Pakistan had lost its opening match of the tournament to the UAE. He also took a swipe at the standard of Pakistan cricket, saying that Sharif's focus on the Hong Kong Sixes reflected the team's current standing.‘Humne Bharat Ko Hara Diya’ bolne ki itni jaldi hai ki fact-check bhi nahin kiya. UAE se haare in the opening game. And also, you can gauge the quality of cricket Pakistan is playing that country’s PM is tweeting about Hong Kong Sixes. I mean. Really!!!" Chopra wrote in an X post.In the match against India, Pakistan captain Abbas Afridi won the toss and elected to bowl. India managed 88/5 in six overs, with Shashank Singh scoring 40 off 11 balls.Pakistan chased down the target of 89 in just 3.5 overs to win by four wickets. Khawaja Nafay top-scored with 41 off 12 balls, while captain Abbas Afridi made 35 off eight deliveries.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
